page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate solid compute capabilities, with average ratings in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests. The CPU supports advanced vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration, which assist in workloads like bzip3 decompression and static web serving, both scoring in the average tier. However, memory performance presents a bottleneck; while cached small-block reads reach 418.63 GB/sec, uncached large-block reads and writes drop to 21.36 GB/sec and 23.88 GB/sec respectively, placing them in the poor and weak performance brackets.

Given its compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, and light text or image processing. It is less suitable for large-scale database operations or medium-to-large language model inference, where its memory bandwidth and capacity limitations result in poor performance.
